sources.title: Project purpose
sources.text:
# Purpose
Orchard coordinates local coding tasks and keeps durable project context for every worker.

sources.title: QueueService architecture
sources.text:
# QueueService architecture
QueueService (QS) owns the durable job queue. SQLite transactions fence owner leases. A worker can publish only while its claim is current.

sources.title: Engineering conventions
sources.text:
# Conventions
Run the focused tests for every behavior change. Keep provider reference material untrusted. Preserve public APIs unless a migration is reviewed.

sources.title: Lease API
sources.text:
# Lease API
export function resumeClaimLease(token: string): boolean
resumeClaimLease validates ownership before renewing the SQLite claim. Never accept an expired token.

sources.title: Restart recovery protocol
sources.text:
# Crash recovery
Recover unfinished jobs after a crash by reconciling persisted claims and reading the last durable checkpoint. Continuing from saved progress avoids repeating completed work.

sources.title: Old queue decision
sources.text:
# Old queue guidance
Before the migration, RetryQueue used process memory. This document is historical and must never be governing context.

sources.title: Current queue decision
sources.text:
# Accepted queue guidance
RetryQueue uses persisted SQLite rows and fenced ownership. The current decision supersedes the old in-memory queue.

sources.title: Deep recovery specification
sources.text:
## Recovery after the appendix
recoverFencedOwnership requires a new claim token and validates the saved checkpoint before resuming.
